attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: We do not yet know whether the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra realizes the required near-parallel two-by-two collar matrices for arbitrary distinct boundary hairpin footprints. Without that, a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor might be invisible to the actual OS test cone.
steps: Start from fixed-collar positivity: for every delta>0 and every finite coefficient vector c, c^*N^delta c>=0; the closed-cone argument is valid after entrywise convergence of these reflected forms.

Collapse the collar and write the most general boundary trace defect still compatible with earlier cycles: N=Gamma\circ M+A. Earlier work showed a positive additive A with zero diagonal must vanish, so the durable obstruction is multiplicative Gamma.
Normalize a two-observable submatrix so N_{11}=N_{22}=M_{11}=M_{22}=1 and set beta=Gamma_{12}. Then N positivity only requires |n|<=1, while intended M positivity requires |n/beta|<=1.

If |beta|<1 and the locked algebra realizes n with |beta|<|n|<=1, the collar matrix N is positive but M has determinant 1-|n/beta|^2<0. This is an actual falsifier, not merely an abstract Schur-multiplier example.

Therefore the previous cycles' statement 'nonrank-one boundary covariance falsifies the bridge' is valid only after adding a realized-richness hypothesis. The proof obligation moves from all positive matrices to the physically realized Wilson OS cone.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a conditional determinant obstruction and a clean promotion criterion, but it does not establish the Yang-Mills analytic input: existence of near-parallel Wilson collar probes with controlled boundary footprints, nor the full no-additive-contact theorem for the relevant nonlocal Wilson products.

assumptions: Fixed-collar reflection positivity is available: every finite matrix N^delta is positive and the RG topology is strong enough to pass its entries to a limiting positive matrix N.
The additive contact part A is positive or at least satisfies the diagonal-zero Cauchy-Schwarz vanishing criterion after diagonal trace continuity has been proved.
For the tested pair, the multiplicative anomaly Gamma is a positive normalized boundary Gram matrix with Gamma_{12}=beta and |beta|<1.

Realized near-parallel testing holds for that pair: after normalizing diagonals, the locked Wilson core realizes a valid collar limit N with |N_{12}|>|beta|, preferably with N_{12} arbitrarily close to the phase of beta.
definitions: source object: finite collar-separated Wilson observable families W_i^delta in the regulated/reflection-positive lattice or continuum cutoff theory, with normalized fixed-collar OS matrices N^delta_{ij}=S_{a,L}(Theta W_i^delta,W_j^delta).
target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(Theta W_i,W_j) on the same gauge-invariant Wilson observables after removing the collar, before adding any boundary label or counterterm.

controlled interface: a collar trace relation N_{ij}=Gamma_{ij} M_{ij}+A_{ij}, with Gamma a normalized multiplicative boundary Gram factor, Gamma_{ii}=1, and A an additive contact matrix forced to vanish when diagonal trace continuity and contact positivity are valid.

same-theory condition: the collar removal map identifies W_i^delta with W_i inside the original gauge-invariant test algebra, allowing only pre-declared individual renormalizations, i.e. diagonal congruences, and forbidding pair-dependent boundary sectors or new reflection-plane observables.

equations.label: collar-limit anomaly decomposition
equations.valid_when: The same regulated Wilson family is used on both sides, the collar limit exists entrywise, and all boundary effects split into a multiplicative Gram factor plus an additive contact term.

equations.label: additive-contact disappearance
equations.valid_when: A is a positive semidefinite contact matrix; then Cauchy-Schwarz gives |A_{ij}|^2\le A_{ii}A_{jj}=0.

equations.label: two-by-two intended determinant
equations.valid_when: The two observables are normalized so N_{11}=N_{22}=M_{11}=M_{22}=1, A=0, beta=Gamma_{12}\ne0, and n=N_{12}.

equations.label: realized determinant falsifier
equations.valid_when: The collar matrix N^{(2)} is an actually realized positive OS matrix and the intended target matrix is obtained by removing the boundary factor without changing the theory.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Try to construct two locked Wilson collar probes with the same bulk observable but distinct boundary hairpin footprints. If their normalized collar OS entry can approach one while the boundary Gram entry beta has |beta|<1, the bridge fails by a concrete 2-by-2 determinant falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma replaces the too-strong universal Schur-multiplier demand by a realized-cone test. It says exactly which part of the Wilson algebra must be rich enough to turn a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor into a same-theory OS-positivity obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let a locked gauge-invariant Wilson core admit collar observables whose fixed-collar OS matrices are positive and whose collar collapse has only a multiplicative boundary Gram factor. For a tested pair, if the normalized anomaly entry satisfies |Gamma_{12}|<1 and the realized collar OS cone contains a normalized two-observable matrix with |N_{12}|>|Gamma_{12}|, then the intended same-theory OS matrix M=Gamma^{[-1]}\circ N has negative determinant. Hence a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor is a genuine falsifier only when the locked algebra realizes such near-parallel two-by-two tests; without that realization, the previous rank-one conclusion overclaims.

assumptions: The two-by-two detector lemma applies to every pair in the finite footprint family.
The realized near-parallel tests are stable under small RG/collar perturbations, so strict determinant negativity is not lost in the limit.
The same-theory observable identification is fixed before proving positivity and does not absorb pair-dependent Gamma entries into new observables.
definitions: Boundary footprint labels are the residual reflection-plane data produced by collapsing reflected Wilson hairpins to t=0.
Near-parallel realization means the collar OS matrix can make two normalized observables arbitrarily correlated in the collar theory while keeping their proposed boundary footprints fixed.
Rank-one harmlessness means Gamma_{ij}=u_i\overline u_j with |u_i|=1 after normalization, so Gamma\circ M=DMD^* and OS positivity is unchanged.

equations.label: pairwise modulus forcing
equations.valid_when: Same-theory OS positivity is required for every realized Wilson pair and additive contacts have vanished.

equations.label: rank-one conclusion for positive normalized Gram
equations.valid_when: The finite Gram matrix is positive semidefinite; equality in every Cauchy-Schwarz pair forces all boundary vectors to be collinear.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If some boundary footprint pair cannot be made near-parallel by any locked Wilson probes, a nonrank-one Gamma may survive without producing a realized determinant violation; then the branch must characterize the smaller physical cone rather than claiming rank-one triviality.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: It gives a promotion route: instead of proving reciprocal Schur positivity on all positive matrices, prove pairwise realized richness on the Wilson core. That is a more plausible Yang-Mills analytic obligation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the locked Wilson core supplies the realized near-parallel test for every pair of boundary footprints in a connected finite family, then any positive multiplicative boundary Gram factor compatible with same-theory OS positivity must have |Gamma_{ij}|=1 for all pairs. Consequently Gamma is rank one on that family and is only a diagonal congruence, so the multiplicative anomaly is harmless.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if repeated attempts fail to realize near-parallel Wilson collar tests and evidence suggests the physical OS cone is intrinsically too small to detect nonrank-one boundary Gram factors.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves pairwise near-parallel realization for a dense locked Wilson core, proves additive contact vanishing there, and shows every boundary Gamma entry must have modulus one, making the collar-to-plane OS bridge valid without changing the theory.
control_decision.reason: The branch made substantive progress by replacing an overbroad rank-one conclusion with a falsifiable realized-cone criterion. The next work is sharply localized and still aligned with the controlled interface.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone passage remains valid for fixed collars, but full collar-to-plane positivity now depends on a realized-cone determinant test rather than universal reciprocal Schur positivity.
The locked Wilson algebra must be rich enough to realize near-parallel two-by-two collar OS tests for boundary footprint pairs; otherwise nonrank-one boundary sectors may be undetectable.
The topology only needs to control the finite reflected matrix entries used in the determinant falsifier/promotion test, not every abstract positive matrix.

falsifiers: A concrete pair of Wilson hairpin footprints with beta=Gamma_{12}, |beta|<1, and an actually realized normalized collar OS entry n satisfying |beta|<|n|<=1 is a determinant falsifier of the same-theory OS bridge.
If additive contact terms are not positive or have nonzero diagonal after diagonal trace locking, then the reduction to multiplicative Gamma is invalid.
If the RG cutoff-removal topology is not strong enough to take the limit of the near-parallel reflected Wilson matrix entries, the determinant test cannot be transported to the continuum.

If the only realized Wilson OS matrices satisfy |N_{12}|<=|Gamma_{12}| whenever |Gamma_{12}|<1, then nonrank-one boundary covariance is not by itself a falsifier; the branch must study the smaller realized cone.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 194 corrects the previous rank-one story in a useful way. The universal Schur-multiplier argument is too strong for Yang-Mills because the theory supplies only realized Wilson OS matrices. The valid bridge lemma is now a realized two-by-two detector: a nonrank-one boundary Gram factor breaks the same-theory OS passage exactly when the locked Wilson core can make collar observables more correlated than the boundary Gram entry allows. This turns the vague richness hypothesis into a concrete determinant experiment and separates formal positivity preservation from the analytic question of whether Wilson hairpin probes are rich enough to see boundary covariance.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Build the simplest Wilson hairpin pair with common bulk loop and distinct boundary footprint labels; compute or bound the normalized collar OS entry n and the boundary Gram beta. The decisive check is whether |n| can be forced above |beta| while the reflected matrix remains a valid collar OS matrix.
